subproblems.title: Rectifiable representations carry no Hⁿ-measure off the support
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Hⁿ(M ∖ spt X) = 0), filled in and stated for an arbitrary representation of an arbitrary current. As in the parent, the vector measure θξHⁿ⌞M is tested against forms φ·b. Two technical substitutions shorten the parent's route:
- instead of (F2) (vanishing on all of U ∖ spt T via a partition of unity), the zero region is covered by countably many open sets W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes;
- instead of passing from C_c^∞ to C_c and then to Borel sets via Riesz uniqueness, Mathlib's fundamental lemma IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero is applied on each W. It accepts an arbitrary measure, so no local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M is needed.
The coordinate covectors dx^I are replaced by an arbitrary finite basis of the covector space. All coefficients are handled as scalar functions; an NVector-valued Bochner integral is avoided on purpose, because at this Mathlib pin no ContinuousENorm instance is found for NVector.
The Lean statement is identical to that of the accepted DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.rectifiable_support_null-a1 (lpf_rectifiable_support_null). This child keeps a fresh name, as this run does for other identical types, so the branch has no cross-branch dependency; the proof below is self-contained.

Notation:
- μ := μHE[n] (= Hⁿ) and ν := μ⌞M = μ.restrict M;
- an n-covector b ∈ Covector (ℝ^P) n is a continuous alternating n-linear map; ‖b‖ is its operator norm, so |b(v₁, …, v_n)| ≤ ‖b‖·∏_i |v_i| (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm);
- e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- 𝒲 is the family of sets W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W, i.e. T(ψ) = 0 for every ψ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ψ ⊆ W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and spt T = T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. (Good points.) By the field orients, for ν-a.e. x there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x) = s·simpleNVector τ. By ae_restrict_mem₀ (M is μ-null-measurable), x ∈ M for ν-a.e. x, and then θ(x) > 0 (field pos). Call x good if both hold; ν-a.e. x is good. For a good x with τ and s as above:
   (a) for every n-covector b, |ξ(x)(b)| = |b(τ₁, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖b‖·∏_i |τ_i| = ‖b‖, since |τ_i| = 1;
   (b) let b_τ := wedgeCovectors n (i ↦ innerSL ℝ τ_i). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, b_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j} = det(Id) = 1, by orthonormality (for n = 0 this is the empty determinant 1). Hence ξ(x)(b_τ) = s ≠ 0, so ξ(x) ≠ 0.
2. (A finite separating family of covectors.) The map Φ : Covector (ℝ^P) n → ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P), Φ(α)(v) := α(e_{v(1)}, …, e_{v(n)}), is ℝ-linear.
   - Φ is injective. If Φ(α) = Φ(β), the alternating maps underlying α and β agree on every tuple of basis vectors, so they are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating with the basis e; a multilinear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors). Hence α = β.
   - The codomain is finite-dimensional, so Covector (ℝ^P) n is finite-dimensional (Module.Finite.of_injective).
   Fix a basis b_1, …, b_N of Covector (ℝ^P) n (Module.finBasis). If w ∈ NVector (ℝ^P) n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors, satisfies w(b_i) = 0 for all i, then w = 0, because a linear map vanishing on a basis is zero (Basis.ext).
3. (Fix W ∈ 𝒲.) K := closure W is compact and K ⊆ U, so θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn), hence on the subset M ∩ W. Since W is open, hence measurable, ν⌞W = μ⌞(W ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Thus θ is ν-integrable on W.
4. (Integrable coefficients.) Fix an n-covector b and put g_b(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(b). Then g_b is ν-integrable on W:
   - x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is ν-a.e. strongly measurable, as the composition of ξ (a.e. strongly measurable for ν by the field aestronglyMeasurable) with the continuous linear evaluation w ↦ w(b) (ContinuousLinearMap.apply);
   - θ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν⌞W (step 3), so g_b is a.e. strongly measurable for ν⌞W;
   - |g_b(x)| ≤ ‖b‖·|θ(x)| for ν-a.e. x, by step 1(a);
   - ‖b‖·|θ| is ν-integrable on W, by step 3.
   Hence IntegrableOn g_b W ν (Integrable.mono'), and in particular LocallyIntegrableOn g_b W ν.
5. (Testing T.) Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ W. The form ω_φ(x) := φ(x)·b is C^∞ with compact support, and tsupport ω_φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U. So ω_φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω_φ ⊆ W, and T(ω_φ) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By the representation hypothesis and the linearity of ξ(x):
   0 = T(ω_φ) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)·b) dμ(x) = ∫ φ(x)·g_b(x) dν(x).
6. (Fundamental lemma.) Steps 4 and 5 are exactly the hypotheses of IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero for the open set W, the measure ν and the function g_b. Hence for ν-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⟹ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) = 0. Since θ(x) > 0 at good points, for ν-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⟹ ξ(x)(b) = 0.
7. (ν(W) = 0.) Apply step 6 to b = b_1, …, b_N and intersect the finitely many full-measure sets with the set of good points (ae_all_iff). For ν-a.e. x, x is good and, if x ∈ W, then ξ(x)(b_i) = 0 for all i, whence ξ(x) = 0 by step 2. This contradicts step 1(b), so ν-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ W, i.e. ν(W) = 0 (ae_iff). Since W is measurable, μ(M ∩ W) = μ(W ∩ M) = ν(W) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply).
8. (Countable union.) Every W ∈ 𝒲 is open and ℝ^P is second countable, so there is a countable subfamily 𝒲₀ ⊆ 𝒲 with ⋃𝒲₀ = ⋃𝒲 = T.zeroRegion (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). Let x ∈ M ∖ spt T. Then x ∈ U (field subset) and x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion, so x ∈ T.zeroRegion, i.e. x ∈ W for some W ∈ 𝒲₀. Hence M ∖ spt T ⊆ ⋃_{W∈𝒲₀} (M ∩ W), a countable union of μ-null sets by step 7. Therefore μ(M ∖ spt T) = 0 (measure_mono_null, measure_biUnion_null_iff). ∎
proof_key_steps: At Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x: θ(x) > 0, |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for every covector b, and ξ(x) ≠ 0, because ξ(x)(b_τ) = ±1 for b_τ = det⟨τ_i, ·⟩.
Covector (ℝ^P) n is finite-dimensional: the coordinate map α ↦ (α(e∘v))_v is injective by Module.Basis.ext_alternating. Hence a finite basis b_1, …, b_N separates n-vectors.
For each open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes and each covector b, θ·ξ(b) is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable on W, and ∫ φ θ ξ(b) d(Hⁿ⌞M) = T(φ·b) = 0 for φ ∈ C_c^∞(W).
The fundamental lemma gives ξ(b_i) = 0 a.e. on W for all i, so ξ = 0 a.e. on W. This contradicts ξ ≠ 0, so Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0.
The zero region is a countable union of such W (second countability), so Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0.

subproblems.title: The Lipschitz push-forward of 3.6 is the classical push-forward for differentiable maps
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), Differentiable ℝ f → IsLipschitzPushforward X f S → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V n) (η : TestFormOn U n), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsLipschitzPushforward: X = τ(M, θ, ξ), f has tangential directional derivatives L(x)v a.e., and S(ω) = ∫_M θ (L_#ξ)(ω∘f) dHⁿ.
By the sibling support-null lemma, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. point of M lies in spt X ⊆ N.
At such points, uniqueness of the derivative of t ↦ f(x + tτ_i) gives L(x) ∘ τ = Df(x) ∘ τ on the orienting frame. Hence (L(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(Df(x)^#ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(η(x)).
The integrands of S(ω) and X(η) agree a.e. on M, so S(ω) = X(η) by integral_congr_ae.

subproblems.title: Pull-back of covectors: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α| for the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q) (α : Covector (Eucl Q) j), covectorEuclideanNorm (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) ≤ ‖L‖ ^ j * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof. The parent justifies (F3) by the singular value decomposition. Transferring that argument to covectorEuclideanNorm, which is defined on continuous alternating maps through the standard basis, would need an SVD factorization L = Σ_i σ_i u_i ⊗ v_i and the orthonormality, for this norm, of the wedges of an arbitrary orthonormal basis. The pinned Mathlib has singular values (LinearMap.singularValues) and an inner product on the abstract exterior power ⋀[ℝ]^n E, but neither the factorization nor any link to covectorEuclideanNorm. The same inequality is therefore proved by the elementary tensor (Hilbert–Schmidt) argument below, which uses only the standard bases.

Notation:
- e_1, …, e_P and e′_1, …, e′_Q are the standard orthonormal bases of ℝ^P and ℝ^Q (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- for i : Fin j → Fin P, e∘i := (e_{i(1)}, …, e_{i(j)}), and similarly e′∘i for i : Fin j → Fin Q;
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, so for a j-covector γ on ℝ^m (m ∈ {P, Q}, with the corresponding standard basis), |γ|² = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²;
- L^#α := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (L^#α)(v₁, …, v_j) = α(Lv₁, …, Lv_j);
- |·| on vectors is the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product, and ‖L‖ the operator norm.

1. (Sum over all index tuples.) For every j-covector γ on ℝ^m: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².
   (a) If i is not injective, e∘i has two equal entries, so γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating.
   (b) The map (I, σ) ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection from pairs (I strictly increasing Fin j → Fin m, σ a permutation of Fin j) onto the injective maps Fin j → Fin m.
      - Surjectivity: for injective i, the tuple i ∘ (sort i) is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing. With I := i ∘ sort i and σ := (sort i)⁻¹, I ∘ σ = i.
      - Injectivity: if I ∘ σ = I′ ∘ σ′, then range I = range I′. A strictly increasing map Fin j → Fin m is determined by its range (it enumerates the range in increasing order), so I = I′, and then σ = σ′ because I is injective.
   (c) For such pairs, γ(e∘(I ∘ σ)) = sign(σ)·γ(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm), so γ(e∘(I ∘ σ))² = γ(e∘I)².
   By (a)–(c), Σ_i γ(e∘i)² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_σ γ(e∘I)² = j!·Σ_I γ(e∘I)² = j!·|γ|², because Fin j has j! permutations.
2. (One slot.) For every linear functional λ : ℝ^Q → ℝ: Σ_{a=1}^{P} λ(Le_a)² ≤ ‖L‖²·Σ_{b=1}^{Q} λ(e′_b)².
   - Put g := Σ_b λ(e′_b)e′_b ∈ ℝ^Q. Then λ(y) = ⟨g, y⟩ for every y (expand y = Σ_b ⟨e′_b, y⟩e′_b), and |g|² = Σ_b λ(e′_b)².
   - Put u := Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a ∈ ℝ^P. Then |u|² = Σ_a λ(Le_a)², and by linearity λ(Lu) = Σ_a λ(Le_a)² = |u|².
   - By Cauchy–Schwarz, |u|² = ⟨g, Lu⟩ ≤ |g|·|Lu| ≤ |g|·‖L‖·|u|.
   Hence |u| ≤ ‖L‖·|g| (trivial if u = 0, otherwise divide by |u|), and squaring gives the claim.
3. (All slots, by induction on j.) For every j ∈ ℕ and every j-multilinear map β : (ℝ^Q)^j → ℝ:
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)})² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   For j = 0 both sides equal β()², because there is exactly one empty tuple and ‖L‖⁰ = 1.
   For the step j → j + 1, write tuples as i = Fin.cons a i′ with a ∈ Fin P and i′ : Fin j → Fin P (and likewise over Fin Q). Write Le∘i′ := (Le_{i′(1)}, …, Le_{i′(j)}).
   - For fixed a, the induction hypothesis applied to the j-multilinear map β(Le_a, ·) gives Σ_{i′} β(Le_a, Le∘i′)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″ : Fin j → Fin Q} β(Le_a, e′∘i″)².
   - Summing over a, the left sides add up to Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j+1)})². After exchanging the finite sums, the right sides add up to ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} Σ_a λ_{i″}(Le_a)², where λ_{i″}(y) := β(y, e′∘i″) is a linear functional on ℝ^Q.
   - By step 2, this is at most ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} ‖L‖²·Σ_b β(e′_b, e′∘i″)² = ‖L‖^{2(j+1)}·Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   This proves the claim for j + 1.
4. (Conclusion.) Apply step 3 to β := α, an alternating and in particular multilinear map. Since (L^#α)(e∘i) = α(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)}), this gives
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} (L^#α)(e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} α(e′∘i)².
   By step 1, applied to L^#α on ℝ^P and to α on ℝ^Q, this reads j!·|L^#α|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·j!·|α|². Dividing by j! > 0 gives |L^#α|² ≤ (‖L‖^j·|α|)². Both |L^#α| and ‖L‖^j·|α| are nonnegative, so |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j·|α|.
   No restriction on j, P, Q is used. For j = 0 both sides equal |α()|; if j > P or j > Q, the corresponding sums over strictly increasing indices are empty. ∎
proof_key_steps: For an alternating γ, the sum of γ(e∘i)² over all index tuples equals j!·|γ|²: non-injective tuples give 0, and injective ones are uniquely permutations of increasing ones.
Single-slot bound Σ_a λ(L e_a)² ≤ ‖L‖² Σ_b λ(e′_b)², via the Riesz vector g of λ, u = Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Induction over the j slots of a multilinear map gives Σ_i α(L e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j} Σ_i α(e′∘i)².
Divide by j! and take square roots: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α|.

subproblems.title: Compatible compactly supported pull-backs exist (cut-off of Simon 2.23)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn V j, ∃ (η : TestFormOn U j) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ζ x • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) ⊆ f ⁻¹' tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F5) of the parent proof (the cut-off function ζ of Simon 2.23, p. 139), filled in. It is stated for an arbitrary set A ⊆ U on which f is proper; the parent uses A = spt X. Neither MapsTo nor openness of V is needed.

Notation: p(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) is the pull-back form f^#ω. C^∞ means smoothness of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. of every finite order.

1. (The compact set.) ω ∈ D^j(V) has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact), and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the properness hypothesis, K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K ⊆ A ⊆ U.
2. (Thickenings.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K, open, with K ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the argument below still applies.
3. (The cut-off.) Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n = ⊤, applied to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s) gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, and ζ = 1 on O;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.
4. (p is C^∞.)
   - x ↦ Df(x) is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
   - x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞ as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω (a test form) and f.
   - B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is C^∞. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors, and it is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
   - Since p(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Df(x)))(ω(f(x))), p is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.clm_apply).
5. (The test form.) Define η(x) := ζ(x)·p(x). η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). Also tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left), so η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport η ⊆ U by step 3. Hence η ∈ D^j(U) = TestFormOn U j, and η(x) = ζ(x)·p(x) for all x by definition.
6. (Support.) If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(f(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence p(x) = 0, the pull-back of the zero covector being zero, and η(x) = 0. So support η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω). This set is closed, since f is continuous and tsupport ω is closed, so tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (closure_minimal).
7. (The open set.) Put N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), an open set. A ⊆ N: for x ∈ A, if f(x) ∈ tsupport ω then x ∈ K ⊆ O; otherwise x ∈ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).
8. (η = p on N.) If x ∈ O ⊆ C, then ζ(x) = 1 and η(x) = p(x). If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then p(x) = 0 = η(x) by step 6.
9. Steps 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 show that η, ζ and N have all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Properness makes K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A a compact subset of the open set U.
Smooth Urysohn on thickenings of K gives a C^∞ cut-off ζ with values in [0, 1], compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood O of K.
The pull-back p = f^#ω is C^∞ (B ↦ B^# is analytic), so η := ζ·p ∈ D^j(U) with tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η = p on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), which contains A.

subproblems.title: Mass comparison for currents related through compatible pull-backs
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, j ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, V ⊆ ℝ^Q, A ⊆ U, Y ∈ D_j(V), Z ∈ D_j(U), and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be of class C^∞ with f⁻¹(K) ∩ A compact for every compact K ⊆ V. Suppose Y(ω) = Z(η) whenever ω ∈ D^j(V), η ∈ D^j(U), and η(x) = (f^#ω)(x) := ω(f(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (Df(x)) for all x in some open set containing A. If c ≥ 0 and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ c for every x, then for every W ⊆ ℝ^Q: M_W(Y) ≤ ofReal(c^j)·M_{f⁻¹(W)∩U}(Z) in [0, ∞], where M is GeometricCurrentOn.massOn.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn V j) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U j) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (c : ℝ), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn V j) (η : TestFormOn U j), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → Y ω = Z η) → 0 ≤ c → (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ c) → ∀ W : Set (Eucl Q), Y.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ j) * Z.massOn (f ⁻¹' W ∩ U)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof. It is stated for an abstract pair (Y, Z) related through compatible pull-backs, so that it applies both to (S, X) in degree k + 1 and to (∂S, ∂X) in degree k, each with A = spt X.

Notation:
- p_ω(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x);
- |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm;
- massAdmissibleOn V j W is the set of ω ∈ D^j(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y;
- Y.massOn W = sup {ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V j W} in [0, ∞], and similarly for Z.

0. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a j-covector β on ℝ^P, |t·β| = |t|·|β|. Indeed (tβ)(e∘I) = t·β(e∘I) for every coefficient, so Σ_I (t·β(e∘I))² = t²·Σ_I β(e∘I)², and √(t²·r) = |t|·√r for r ≥ 0 (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
1. Fix W ⊆ ℝ^Q. Since Y.massOn W is a supremum (sSup_le), it suffices to show ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(c^j)·Z.massOn(f⁻¹(W) ∩ U) for every ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V j W. Fix such an ω.
2. (Compatible form.) Apply the sibling lemma iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm to ω, using U open, A ⊆ U, f C^∞ and properness on A. It gives η ∈ D^j(U), ζ with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, and an open N ⊇ A such that:
   - η(x) = ζ(x)·p_ω(x) for all x;
   - η = p_ω on N;
   - tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
   The compatibility hypothesis, applied to ω, η and N, gives Y(ω) = Z(η).
3. (Support.) tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ f⁻¹(W), because tsupport ω ⊆ W. Also tsupport η ⊆ U, because η ∈ D^j(U). Hence tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(W) ∩ U.
4. (Pointwise bound.) For every x,
   |η(x)| = |ζ(x)|·|p_ω(x)| ≤ |p_ω(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^j·|ω(f(x))| ≤ c^j·1 = c^j.
   This uses step 0 with |ζ(x)| ≤ 1, the sibling lemma iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le, |ω(f(x))| ≤ 1, and ‖Df(x)‖^j ≤ c^j (from 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ c; pow_le_pow_left₀).
5. (Case c^j = 0.) Then j ≠ 0, because c^0 = 1, and c = 0 (pow_eq_zero_iff). So ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ 0, i.e. Df(x) = 0, for every x. Then p_ω(x) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap 0 = 0, because the j-linear map ω(f(x)) with j ≥ 1 vanishes when an argument is 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_coord_zero). So η(x) = ζ(x)·0 = 0 for all x, η = 0 in D^j(U), and Y(ω) = Z(0) = 0 by linearity. Therefore ofReal(Y(ω)) = 0 ≤ ofReal(c^j)·Z.massOn(f⁻¹(W) ∩ U).
6. (Case c^j > 0.) Put η₁ := (c^j)⁻¹·η ∈ D^j(U).
   - tsupport η₁ ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(W) ∩ U (tsupport_smul_subset_right and step 3);
   - |η₁(x)| = (c^j)⁻¹·|η(x)| ≤ 1, by steps 0 and 4.
   So η₁ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U j (f⁻¹(W) ∩ U), and ofReal(Z(η₁)) ≤ Z.massOn(f⁻¹(W) ∩ U) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since η = c^j·η₁, linearity gives Z(η) = c^j·Z(η₁). Using ENNReal.ofReal_mul with c^j ≥ 0:
   ofReal(Y(ω)) = ofReal(c^j·Z(η₁)) = ofReal(c^j)·ofReal(Z(η₁)) ≤ ofReal(c^j)·Z.massOn(f⁻¹(W) ∩ U).
7. Steps 1, 5 and 6 give Y.massOn W ≤ ofReal(c^j)·Z.massOn(f⁻¹(W) ∩ U). This holds also when the right-hand mass is ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each ω admissible for M_W(Y), the compatible-form sibling gives η = ζ·f^#ω ∈ D^j(U) with Y(ω) = Z(η) and tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(W) ∩ U.
The pull-back norm sibling and 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 give |η(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖^j |ω(f x)| ≤ c^j.
If c^j = 0, then j ≥ 1 and Df ≡ 0, so η = 0 and Y(ω) = 0. Otherwise η/c^j is admissible for M_{f⁻¹(W)∩U}(Z), so ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(c^j)·M_{f⁻¹(W)∩U}(Z).
Take the supremum over ω.

subproblems.title: Boundary commutes with smooth push-forward (Simon 2.24(1))
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q, X ∈ D_{k+1}(U), S ∈ D_{k+1}(V), and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be of class C^∞. Suppose S(ω′) = X(η′) whenever ω′ ∈ D^{k+1}(V), η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(U) and η′ = f^#ω′ on some open set containing spt X. Then ∂S(ω) = ∂X(η) whenever ω ∈ D^k(V), η ∈ D^k(U) and η = f^#ω on some open set containing spt X. Here (f^#ω)(x) := ω(f(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (Df(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V (k + 1)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ (ω : TestFormOn V (k + 1)) (η : TestFormOn U (k + 1)), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (k + 1)) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) (k + 1)) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η) → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V k) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) k) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S.boundary ω = X.boundary η
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon 2.24(1): ∂f_#T = f_#∂T), with the degree-(k+1) formula as hypothesis. The formula is applied directly to dω and dη on the same open set. This shortens the parent's step 5, which goes through an auxiliary η′ from (F5) and the support fact (F2); neither is needed.

Notation:
- p_ω(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x);
- for ψ ∈ D^k(U) (resp. D^k(V)), dψ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k ψ ∈ D^{k+1}(U) (resp. with V); its underlying form is extDeriv ψ;
- by definition ∂S(ω) = S(dω) and ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).

1. Fix ω ∈ D^k(V), η ∈ D^k(U) and an open N ⊇ spt X with η(x) = p_ω(x) for every x ∈ N. Then dω ∈ D^{k+1}(V) and dη ∈ D^{k+1}(U).
2. (Locality.) Let x ∈ N. Since N is open, η = p_ω on a neighbourhood of x, i.e. η =ᶠ[𝓝 x] p_ω (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence extDeriv η x = extDeriv p_ω x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq): extDeriv ψ x is the alternatization of fderiv ℝ ψ x, which depends only on the germ of ψ at x.
3. (Naturality.) ω is C^∞, being a test form, so it is differentiable at f(x). f is C^∞, so ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ f x, and minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2 ≤ ∞. Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback therefore gives
   extDeriv p_ω x = (extDeriv ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) = Df(x)^#((dω)(f(x))).
4. By steps 2–3, (dη)(x) = Df(x)^#((dω)(f(x))) for every x ∈ N. So dη agrees with the pull-back of dω on the open set N ⊇ spt X. The hypothesis, applied with ω′ := dω, η′ := dη and the same N, gives S(dω) = X(dη).
5. Hence ∂S(ω) = S(dω) = X(dη) = ∂X(η). ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂S(ω) = S(dω) and ∂X(η) = X(dη) by the definition of the boundary.
Locality of extDeriv on the open set N where η = f^#ω, together with Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback (naturality of d), gives dη = f^#(dω) on N.
Applying the degree-(k+1) formula to (dω, dη, N) gives ∂S(ω) = X(dη) = ∂X(η).
